h1: Custom Nursing Scrubs for Healthcare Teams
metaDescription: Order custom nursing scrubs for your team. Durable, comfortable, and available in bulk. Get a quote today at Perfect Imprints.
introHtml:
Marketing directors and HR managers in healthcare know that a unified team look builds trust with patients and pride among staff. Custom nursing scrubs do more than identify your team — they project professionalism and comfort during long shifts. Whether you're outfitting a new hospital wing, rebranding a clinic network, or supplying a nursing school cohort, you need scrubs that hold up to daily wear and frequent washing. Our catalog includes top-selling styles like the Rugby Polo and Safety Tee, plus practical accessories like the Shoe Caddy and BeWell™ Socks that complete the uniform. We offer screen printing and embroidery to add your logo or facility name, with minimum quantities that work for departments of any size.

Safety managers also turn to custom nursing scrubs for their durability and visibility options. The Safety Tee and Fleece Gloves provide extra coverage in cooler environments, while accessories like the COB Headlamp and Retro Specs add function beyond the uniform. From a single unit for a sample to bulk orders of hundreds, we help you choose the right fabric weights, pocket configurations, and decoration methods. Our team guides you through sizing, care instructions, and lead times so your order arrives ready for the first shift. Start with a quote and we'll match your budget and timeline.
buyingGuideHtml:
When ordering custom nursing scrubs for your team, focus on fabric quality and fit. Most scrubs are made from cotton-polyester blends or performance fabrics with stretch. Look for moisture-wicking materials that keep staff comfortable during long shifts. Reinforced seams and ample pocket space are practical features that nurses appreciate. Avoid fabrics that shrink excessively — pre-shrunk options are worth the investment for bulk orders.

Materials and Durability

Polyester-cotton blends offer a balance of breathability and wrinkle resistance. Performance fabrics with spandex provide stretch for bending and lifting. For colder environments, consider fleece-lined options like the Fleece Gloves or layered looks with the Winterdana. Check the care label: scrubs that survive industrial laundering save your team replacement costs. Many suppliers offer thread counts and weight specifications — ask for swatches before placing a large order.

Common Use Cases

Custom nursing scrubs are used in hospitals, clinics, dental offices, veterinary practices, and nursing schools. Marketing directors order them for branded uniforms at trade shows and community health fairs. HR directors use them for employee onboarding kits. Safety managers choose high-visibility styles for emergency response teams. Accessories like the Shoe Caddy and BeWell™ Socks make great add-ons for year-end appreciation gifts or conference swag bags.

Decoration and Customization

Screen printing works well for simple logos on cotton-rich fabrics. Embroidery is durable and looks professional on polo-style scrubs like the Rugby Polo. For full-color designs, heat transfer or sublimation is ideal on polyester blends. Keep in mind that pocket placement and seam lines can affect decoration placement. Always request a proof before production to avoid misalignment. Branded nursing scrubs with a logo on the chest or sleeve create a cohesive team identity.

Quantity and MOQ Guidance

Minimum order quantities for custom nursing scrubs typically start at 12 to 24 pieces per style and color. Bulk orders of 50 or more reduce per-unit costs significantly. For large teams, consider ordering extra stock for turnover. Wholesale pricing is available for orders over 100 units. If you need a mix of sizes, order a size run to ensure everyone gets a good fit. Sample programs let you test fabric and fit before committing to the full run.

Avoiding Common Mistakes

One common mistake is ordering the wrong size ratio. Request a size distribution chart from your team before ordering. Another pitfall is choosing a fabric that doesn't match the work environment — heavy scrubs may be too hot for summer, while thin scrubs may not last through frequent washing. Also, confirm lead times: custom embroidery can add 5-10 business days. Finally, order a small test batch if you're trying a new supplier or decoration method. Personalized nursing scrubs that fit well and wear well keep your team looking professional shift after shift.

faqs.q: What is the minimum order quantity for custom nursing scrubs?
faqs.a: Minimum order quantities typically start at 12 to 24 pieces per style and color. For smaller teams, we can sometimes accommodate lower quantities with a setup fee. Contact us for details.

faqs.q: What decoration methods are available for nursing scrubs?
faqs.a: We offer screen printing, embroidery, and heat transfer. Embroidery is durable and professional for logos on polo-style scrubs. Screen printing works well for larger designs on cotton blends. Full-color heat transfer is ideal for polyester fabrics.

faqs.q: How long does production take for custom scrubs?
faqs.a: Standard production takes 10-15 business days after proof approval. Embroidery may add 5-7 days. Rush orders are available for an additional fee. Shipping time depends on your location.

faqs.q: Can I order a sample before placing a bulk order?
faqs.a: Yes, we offer sample programs. You can order a single unit of a style to check fabric, fit, and color. Sample costs are often credited toward your bulk order.

faqs.q: What fabrics are best for nursing scrubs?
faqs.a: Cotton-polyester blends are breathable and easy to care for. Performance fabrics with spandex offer stretch and comfort. For durability, look for reinforced seams and pre-shrunk materials. We can provide swatches to help you decide.
